subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should arbitrary first-time plugin installs fail closed unless they resolve through ClawHub or OpenClaw-owned bundled/catalog metadata, while existing updates and selected guided flows remain exempt?
rationale: Source and dependency review support the implementation, but choosing warning-free executable sources and deliberately breaking unattended callers requires maintainer security and compatibility intent.

options.title: Approve current trust model
options.body: Keep exact source classification, interactive warnings, the separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and the documented trusted-flow exemptions.

options.title: Narrow the policy
options.body: Trust fewer source classes or exempt fewer entry points, then update focused fresh-install and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Preserve unattended defaults
options.body: Make strict provenance acknowledgement opt-in rather than changing existing noninteractive first-install behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve current trust model
recommendation.body: Keep exact source classification, interactive warnings, the separate noninteractive acknowledgement, chat restrictions, and the documented trusted-flow exemptions.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main merged history covers both central plugin-install and Crestodian code paths affected by the decision.
